title: Squares on a Chessboard
prompt: How many squares are there on a standard 8×8 chessboard?
Count squares of all sizes — not just the 64 individual cells.
hints: Don't just count 1×1 squares. A 2×2 region of cells is also a square. So is a 3×3, 4×4, and so on up to 8×8.
Count each size separately. How many different positions can a 2×2 square occupy on the board? How about a 3×3?
An k×k square can be placed in (9-k)² different positions. Sum this for k = 1 through 8.
solution_lede:
The 64 individual cells are just the 1×1 squares. But a chessboard contains squares of every size from 1×1 up to 8×8.

A k×k square can be positioned with its top-left corner anywhere in a (9−k) × (9−k) grid of positions. So:
1×1: 8² = 64
2×2: 7² = 49
3×3: 6² = 36
4×4: 5² = 25
5×5: 4² = 16
6×6: 3² = 9
7×7: 2² = 4
8×8: 1² = 1

Total = 1² + 2² + 3² + … + 8² = 204.

solution_steps.body: A k×k square fits in (9−k)² positions on the board. Count each size: 64, 49, 36, 25, 16, 9, 4, 1.
This is the sum of squares: 1² + 2² + … + 8² = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6 with n=8.
